text: Exome sequencing of 14 brainstem gliomas (BSGs) and 12 thalamic gliomas, plus targeted mutational analysis of 24 additional tumors and genome-wide methylation profiling of 45 gliomas, identified tumor-specific PPM1D mutations in 37.5% of BSGs carrying hallmark H3F3A p.Lys27Met substitutions. PPM1D encodes wild-type p53-induced protein phosphatase 1D (WIP1). PPM1D mutations were mutually exclusive with TP53 mutations in BSG and attenuated p53 activation in vitro. The mutations were truncating alterations in exon 6 that enhanced PPM1D's ability to suppress activation of the DNA damage response checkpoint protein CHK2. These results define PPM1D as a frequent target of somatic mutation and a potential therapeutic target in brainstem gliomas.
